business_summary: Microsoft sells software, cloud computing and devices to businesses, governments and consumers. FY2026 (ended 2026-06-30) revenue was $331.839B, up 18% from $281.724B, across three reported segments: Productivity & Business Processes (Microsoft 365, Teams, LinkedIn, Dynamics) $139.996B; Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, GitHub) $137.791B; More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface, search advertising) $54.052B. Azure passed $100B of annual revenue for the first time in FY2026 and grew 43% in Q4. Most revenue is recurring subscription or consumption-based, and commercial remaining performance obligation (contracted future revenue) reached $678B, up 84%. From FY2027 Microsoft reports in two new segments, 'Agents and Infra' ($268.1B FY2026 revenue recast) and 'Devices and Consumer' ($63.7B). The business should still be winning in 5-10 years because enterprises run their operations on Microsoft software, switching costs are very high, and Microsoft is one of a handful of credible platforms for the AI buildout. The open question this year is not demand but capital intensity: cash capex nearly doubled to $115.948B in FY2026 (plus $24.608B of finance-lease right-of-use assets), so free cash flow FELL to $66.987B from $71.611B even as revenue grew 18%. REFRESH NOTE 2026-10-24: no new financial filing since the 2026-09-02 8-K (only Form 4s, the 2026-10-21 proxy and annual report). Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-09-30) results are due after the close on Wednesday 2026-10-28, so the fundamental numbers here still reflect FY2026 (fiscal year ended 2026-06-30). Starting with that report Microsoft will report under its new 'Agents and Infra' / 'Devices and Consumer' segments.

moat.type: High switching costs (Microsoft 365, Windows, Azure, Dynamics), network effects (Teams, LinkedIn, GitHub), scale economies in cloud infrastructure, deep enterprise distribution and contracted backlog

quality.roic: ~31% estimated: NOPAT $125.1B (operating income $155.237B x (1 - 19.4% effective tax rate)) on average invested capital ~$405.3B (equity + total debt + finance-lease liabilities - cash and short-term investments, FY2025/FY2026 average). Derived from 10-K figures, not a reported metric.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: ~0.15x. Net cash of $36.5B excluding leases ($76.843B cash + short-term investments vs $40.294B total debt); including $66.594B of finance-lease liabilities, net debt is ~$30.0B against EBITDA of ~$199.6B (operating income $155.237B + depreciation $34.3B + intangible amortization $4.7B + finance-lease ROU amortization $5.403B). Finance-lease liabilities have grown from $27.145B (FY2024) to $66.594B (FY2026) and are the fastest-growing obligation on the balance sheet.
quality.fcf_positive: yes, but shrinking: FY2026 FCF $66.987B (operating cash flow $182.935B - capex $115.948B), down from $71.611B in FY2025. Net of $3.101B finance-lease principal payments, $63.886B.

valuation.method: Blend (simple average) of two methods run through code/valuation.py, INPUTS UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-17 thesis because no new filing has been released since (per the 2026-09-17 playbook lesson, we do not move fair value without a changed, cited fundamental). (1) P/E: 26x / 30x / 34x on FY2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $17.28 -> $449.28 / $518.40 / $587.52. 30x is a reasonable base for a wide-moat ~18% grower with ~47% operating margins; 26x covers a de-rating if the AI capex disappoints, 34x continued AI-driven acceleration. (2) FCF yield: 3.8% / 3.2% / 2.7% on FY2026 FCF per share $8.99 ($66.987B / 7,453M diluted shares) -> $236.58 / $280.94 / $332.96. Blended band $342.93 / $399.67 / $460.24. Margin of safety at $524.38 = -31.2% (NEGATIVE; the price is about 14% ABOVE the HIGH end of the band). SENSITIVITY, stated honestly: (a) on trailing P/E alone the stock is roughly fair - $524.38 is 30.3x FY2026 non-GAAP EPS, right at our 30x base. (b) Using the aggregator consensus FY2027 non-GAAP EPS of $19.78 (stockanalysis.com, 2026-10-23; NOT filing-backed) at the same 26/30/34x gives $514 / $593 / $673, and the stock would look 'fair, leaning cheap' (+11.6% margin). That forward view is informational only and is NOT used in the band. (c) The whole gap between 'roughly fair' and '31% overvalued' comes from the free-cash-flow method: cash capex ($115.9B) was 3.4x depreciation ($34.3B) in FY2026 and FCF per share is only $8.99, a 1.7% FCF yield at today's price. Whether that capex earns a return is not knowable yet. We keep the cash-flow method in deliberately. (d) Wall Street consensus 12-month target is ~$592-$599 (MarketBeat via Tradingpedia / stockanalysis.com, Oct 2026); we note it but do not anchor on it, because sell-side targets are mostly forward-P/E based and ignore the FCF disagreement.

bull_case: Wide moat intact and arguably widening: commercial remaining performance obligation (contracted future revenue) jumped 84% to $678B in Q4 FY2026.

Azure passed $100B of annual revenue in FY2026 and grew 43% in Q4; management guided Q1 FY2027 Azure growth of 44-45% constant currency, i.e. acceleration at enormous scale. Q1 FY2027 will be the first quarter in which Microsoft discloses Azure revenue in dollars. Recast FY2026 Azure revenue was $101.9B.
Exceptional economics: 67.9% gross margin, 46.8% operating margin, ~31% estimated ROIC, net cash of $36.5B excluding leases (FY2026 10-K).

AI is monetising: Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats (reported 2026-07-29), up from 15 million in January 2026 and over 20 million in April 2026 per press coverage of management commentary.

Sell-side is overwhelmingly positive: consensus FY2027 non-GAAP EPS ~$19.78 (+14% vs FY2026's $17.28) and a ~$599 average 12-month price target from ~56 analysts (aggregator data, Oct 2026). On that forward view the stock looks fairly priced.
risks: VALUATION IS THE PRIMARY RISK: at $524.38 MSFT trades 31% above our base fair value of $399.67 and ~14% above the $460.24 high end. The stock rose from $497.58 (2026-09-17) to $524.38 with no new fundamental data, so the margin of safety has worsened by ~7 percentage points purely from price. FCF yield at today's price is ~1.7% ($8.99 / $524.38).

BINARY EVENT IN 4 DAYS: Q1 FY2027 results land 2026-10-28 after the close. The bar is high (Azure 44-45% cc guide vs ~41% Street before the guide; Q1 capex guided >$50B). Press reports note that in January 2026 Azure grew 38% and the stock still fell ~10%. Any price we see before 10-28 reflects expectations, not results.

Free cash flow is going backwards: FY2026 FCF $66.987B vs $71.611B in FY2025 despite +18% revenue, because cash capex rose from $64.551B to $115.948B; Q1 FY2027 capex is guided above $50B on its own, so FY2027 FCF could fall again (a third year of decline would trip a sell trigger).
The AI capex bet is unproven: capex is 3.4x depreciation, so today's margins are flattered relative to the depreciation this asset base will eventually carry.
Debt-like leases are building: finance-lease liabilities $27.145B (FY2024) -> $46.172B (FY2025) -> $66.594B (FY2026), outside the headline 'net cash' figure.
Earnings quality: FY2026 GAAP net income included a $3.2B gain on the Anthropic investment; mark-to-market gains on AI stakes are not repeatable operating profit.

Copilot monetisation per seat is not disclosed: Microsoft reports seat counts, not Copilot revenue, and press reports describe promotional pricing and possible volume discounts (unverified). Seat growth may come at lower revenue per seat.
Macro and rates: the 2026-09 thesis recorded fed funds at 3.75-4.00% and CPI 3.4% (not re-verified in this refresh). Higher rates compress multiples on long-duration growth stocks.
Regulatory/antitrust scrutiny in the US and EU over cloud bundling, the OpenAI relationship and AI market power.

Segment reporting change from Q1 FY2027 reduces comparability with history; Azure is being redefined (GitHub and Security Copilot move out; recast FY2026 Azure $101.9B), so growth rates may not be like-for-like.
what_would_break_thesis: Azure constant-currency revenue growth falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (guidance for Q1 FY2027 is 44-45%; a fall to sub-20% would mean the AI cloud thesis has broken).
Total company revenue declines year over year for two consecutive quarters.
Company-wide gross margin falls below 60% for two consecutive quarters (FY2026: 67.9%).
Operating margin falls below 38% for two consecutive quarters (FY2026: 46.8%) - the signal that AI capex depreciation is overwhelming the P&L.
Free cash flow declines year over year for a third consecutive fiscal year, or turns negative for any full fiscal year (FY2025 $71.6B -> FY2026 $67.0B is already one year of decline).
Net-debt-to-EBITDA including finance-lease liabilities rises above 1.5x (currently ~0.15x), or finance-lease liabilities exceed $150B.
Estimated ROIC falls below 15% on a sustained multi-year basis (currently ~31%).
Commercial remaining performance obligation declines year over year.

A serious accounting restatement, an SEC enforcement action, or a material governance red flag - in particular any restatement of datacentre asset useful lives or of revenue recognised on AI-related related-party transactions.
catalysts: Q1 FY2027 earnings Wednesday 2026-10-28 after the close (webcast 2:30pm PT): tests the 44-45% Azure guide, the >$50B capex guide, the first-ever dollar Azure disclosure, and FY2027 FCF trajectory. This thesis must be refreshed by 2026-10-30.
Evidence of return on AI capex: Agents and Infra operating margin holding up as FY2026-27 build-out depreciation hits the P&L.
A price pullback toward the $400 base or $343 low of our band. The 250-day low on our Alpaca feed is $352.42, so it is not an impossible price.
Capex growth normalising toward depreciation, which would lift reported FCF sharply and resolve the earnings-vs-cash-flow disagreement in our valuation.
Copilot paid seats compounding well beyond 30 million without heavy discounting.
